# order: EO:2065  (WPA 1944: 1914 Oct 27)
# WPA summary: Margaret A. Hampton, clerk in the Census Bureau, Com merce Dept., made eligiblefor transfer as clerk to the Children's Bu reau, Labor Dept. 1915 CSR 117.
# book: Thirty-second Annual Report of the United States Civil Service Commission, fiscal year ended June 30, 1915
# scanned image 124, printed page 117; page lines 12-24
# source: https://archive.org/download/annualreportuni01commgoog/annualreportuni01commgoog_djvu.xml  sha256 92d8549007f776879ba70597db655a8e2deb53a49329d0574b35f0591c6fb041
# found by: monthday_and_names; date 1914-10-27; words margaret|hampton|children's
# Government printed copy (OCR of a compilation or report), not the signed original. A lead for the
# original_text step: read it against the scan before use. Exact slice of the page OCR follows.
----- EXACT SLICE -----
mend her to the Secretary of the Treasury for appointment to such a position.
The Civil Service Commission does not recommend that an order be issued in this
case.
October 27, 1014.
Mrs. Margaret A. Hampton may be transferred from the position of clerk at $1,000
per annum m the Census Bureau, Department of Commerce, to the position of clerk at
$1,200 per annum in the Children's Bureau, Department oi Labor, without regard to
the requirements of the civil-service rules.
Mrs. Hampton was appointed temporary clerk in the Thirteenth Census on April 1,
1910, and served \mtil July 1. 1912, when she received a permanent appointment as
clerk at $1,000 per annum tnrough Executive order. Sne has rendered excellent
service with the Census Bureau, and her transfer to the Children's Bureau is recom-
mended by the Secretsuy of Labor and the chief of the Children's Bureau.
